cards.text: One Sabbath, Jesus is passing through the grainfields with His disciples. As they walk along, the disciples start picking heads of grain. Nobody stops walking, they just reach, like my mustache EVERY time I pass the chocolate chip station.

cards.question: The disciples are picking grain as they walk through the fields on the Sabbath. Who speaks up about it?
The Pharisees tell Jesus to look at what His disciples are doing in the grainfield. What's their problem with it?

answers.text: It is unlawful on the Sabbath

cards.text: Jesus answers with a question about David, who later became Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3): "Have you never read what David did when he and his companions were hungry and in need?" Asking the Pharisees if they've read the Scriptures is like asking ME if I've ever heard of an oven.

cards.question: Jesus says that during the high priesthood of Abiathar, a hungry David entered the house of God. What did David eat there?
The consecrated bread David ate in the house of God was lawful only for the priests.

cards.text: And David didn't keep that bread to himself. He gave some to his companions as well, which is more than I can say for me and a fresh cooling rack.

cards.question: After the story about David, Jesus declares who the Sabbath was made for. What does He say?

answers.text: The Sabbath was made for man
The Sabbath was made for kings
The Sabbath was made for priests

cards.question: Jesus keeps going. Because the Sabbath was made for man, He says someone is Lord even of the Sabbath. Who?

cards.text: Son of Man is how Jesus talks about Himself (Mark 2:10), so the Pharisees just tried to explain the Sabbath to its Lord. Friend, that's like explaining the oven to the guy who BUILT the bakery.

Once again Jesus goes into the synagogue on a Sabbath, and a man with a withered hand is there. Friend, I know a little about parts that stop working, my old edges got so blurry my cookies looked like WEATHER MAPS.

cards.question: A man with a withered hand is in the synagogue, and some people there are watching Jesus. What are they watching for?

answers.text: If He will heal on the Sabbath
If He will read from the scroll
If He will teach the crowd

cards.question: The people watching Jesus in the synagogue are hoping the man with the withered hand will get help.

cards.text: So they're watching in order to accuse Him, and Jesus says to the man with the withered hand, "Stand up among us." Right in the middle of everybody, which, for a guy who spent years in the back of a junk drawer, sounds TERRIFYING.

cards.question: With the man standing among them, Jesus asks which is lawful on the Sabbath. What is the first pair of choices He gives?

answers.text: To do good or to do evil

cards.question: Jesus asks the people watching Him whether it's lawful on the Sabbath to do good or evil, to save life or destroy it. How do they answer?

cards.text: They are silent, so quiet you could hear a sprinkle drop. Jesus looks around at them with anger and sorrow at their hardness of heart.

cards.question: Jesus says to the man, "Stretch out your hand." The man stretches it out, and his hand is ___.
After Jesus restores the man's hand, the Pharisees go out. Who do they start plotting with?
The Pharisees and the Herodians begin plotting how they might ___ Jesus.

findings.problem: The Pharisees first show up here, as the answer to this card, and no card ever says who they are. Card 3, card 4 and card 10 all name them without an introduction. A card after this pick, like card 3's question or the next story card, should briefly say who the Pharisees are.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The Herodians first show up here, as the answer to this card. The walkthrough ends right after, so no card ever says who they are.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: In stop 1, 5 of the 6 choice cards are multiple choice, with 1 true or false and no fill in the blank. Cards 2 and 3 are back-to-back multiple choice, and so are cards 8 and 9. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The second half of Jesus' declaration in Mark 2:27, "not man for the Sabbath," is never told on any card. Card 8 asks only "made for man," and card 9 skips straight to the Son of Man. This half is key to what Jesus means, so the baker leaves without an important detail.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The card states as fact that the watchers weren't hoping the man would get help. Mark 3:2 gives only their purpose ("In order to accuse Jesus"), not what they hoped for the man. The answer False rests on a feeling the text doesn't state, and a baker could argue it either way. Ask about their stated purpose instead.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The joke makes the Pharisees the butt ("the Pharisees just tried to explain the Sabbath to its Lord... like explaining the oven to the guy who BUILT the bakery"). It laughs at them, not with their human situation, and Papa Dorin isn't the one being laughed at.

rule.text: Humble. When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself. Humor about people in Bible stories laughs with their human situation, never at them.
